messages:
Sam W: Quick Q — Atlas Health wants a Private deployment POC. They require PrivateLink into their corporate VPC and an on‑prem TLS inspection proxy. Two asks: preserve client source IP for audit, and a static egress IP (for their firewall allowlist). Any immediate blockers on our side?
Jess P: Thanks Sam. Do they need TLS termination on our side or passthrough to their proxy? That changes how we preserve src IP.
Sam W: They said their on‑prem proxy will do L7 inspection (they want us to connect from our Private nodes to the proxy). Ideally we keep original client IP for logging upstream.
Tyler N: Short answer: passthrough (TCP) keeps original client IP only if there's no NAT along the path. With PrivateLink (interface endpoints) traffic originates from our ENIs in the customer account, so we'll have our Private deployment nodes' IPs as source — not the end user IP.
Maria L: Alternatives: 1) Mutual TLS passthrough via a tunnel where customer terminates TLS — this preserves client IP if the customer’s on‑prem ingress preserves it. 2) If they need TLS termination on our side (we terminate and reencrypt), upstream will see our node IPs; we can add X-Forwarded-For but that requires the customer's proxy to trust/report it.
Tyler N: For PrivateLink specifically: traffic flow = our infra -> interface endpoint -> customer VPC -> their proxy. Customer sees our ENI IPs. To preserve the end client IPs you'd need the on‑prem proxy to ingest headers we set, or use a client‑side direct connection (not PrivateLink).
Jess P: Ok so we should surface two options to the customer: PrivateLink + header propagation (doc their trust model), or VPC peering/transit path that preserves original src IP but requires more network changes. Which is quicker?
Maria L: PrivateLink is faster to provision and lower blast radius — recommended for POC. For audit requirements, ask if XFF header is acceptable. Otherwise peering/transit (VPN/Direct) might be needed but takes longer and needs their infra changes.
Sam W: They asked about firewall rules and port lists — can we give a concise allowlist they can paste into their ticket?
Tyler N: Yes. Minimal outbound from customer to us (for PrivateLink): allow ephemeral TCP to our service ports (443 + optional 8443). Example snippet: ```Allow from customer-proxy -> our-endpoint ENI: TCP 443 (TLS)``` For our egress static IPs (if they want to allowlist our egress): we can provide a short list of NAT EIP(s) per region. For POC we'll allocate a single EIP.
Maria L: Concrete allowlist example to include in ticket: ```Customer inbound rules (to their proxy): allow 10.0.1.0/24 -> proxy:443 Protocol: TCP``````Our egress IPs that customer should allow: 54.23.177.88/32 (POC EIP, sample)``` Note: replace sample EIP with assigned EIP in handoff.
Jess P: Great. Any pricing or contract blockers for Private deployment POC?
Sam W: They asked about pricing for Private license + reserved nodes and egress.
Maria L: For POC we usually do a time‑boxed eval: short private deploy trial (30 days) with small commit. Pricing components: private deployment license (one‑time or monthly), reserved GPU capacity (monthly pro‑rata), public egress bandwidth (cloud provider rates) + optional professional services. I can send a ballpark in a DM.
Jess P: Customer also submitted a security questionnaire — they want short answers for networking items (TLS termination, key management, audit logs). Can we provide quick bullets?
Tyler N: Sure — sample answers: - TLS: TLS1.2+ enforced, mTLS optional for control plane. - KMS: Customer-managed KMS supported (bring your own key) via our Private control plane integrations. - Audit logs: We stream audit logs to customer destination (S3/CloudWatch) in Private deployments. - Network segmentation: Deployment runs in customer VPC with security groups and NACLs they control.
Sam W: Perfect. I'll paste that into the questionnaire and follow up. Any operational caveats we should tell the customer?
Maria L: Caveats: - If they require source IP preservation for end‑user telemetry, PrivateLink will not by itself preserve end user IPs — need header propagation or a different topology. - SNI rewrite / TLS inspection in the middle will break cert pinning; if customer insists on MITM it must be part of their control plane. - We can do canary rollouts in Private with the same rollback policies as hosted.
ops-bot: Deployment note: created POC ticket #POC-7891, assigned to eng‑oncall. ETA network presubmit: 48 hours. :white_check_mark:
Jess P: :thumbsup: I'll loop in their network team and request confirmation on X-Forwarded-For acceptance + which approach they prefer (PrivateLink or peering).
Sam W: Thanks all — I'll update Atlas Health and post back once they confirm headers / EIP acceptance. :eyes:
